observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: HIMALAYA_TIBET_CORE: 33 tagged to collision-belt family; 13 PB2002 Persia–Tibet–Burma orogen events outside original boxes; 7 Myanmar geometric overlap events are Burma/Shan-Thai tags, not Himalaya-core candidates.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP AS A COLLISION-BELT CANDIDATE; define west/central/east orogen boundaries from published tectonic segmentation. Do not merge all Pamir/Hindukush/Afghan events by proximity alone.
source_derived_tectonic_context: Himalaya, Tibetan Plateau and Pamir–Hindukush deformation form a complex collision system; slab geometries and seismicity differ by sector.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Use a published polygon or tectonic transect definition; distinguish crustal collision earthquakes from intermediate-depth Hindu Kush/Pamir seismicity using depth, focal mechanism and slab evidence.
supporting_references: Nature Reviews (2021); Lithosphere review (2021); Nature Reviews (2025).

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: Seven Myanmar overlap events: 4 Burma and 3 Shan-Thai; the GIS audit also identifies 13 PB2002 Persia–Tibet–Burma orogen events outside all original windows and 1 such event inside the Sunda box.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP SEPARATE FROM BOTH HIMALAYA CORE AND SUNDA ARC; retain as complex transition system with possible subdomains: Indo-Burman subduction/collision, Sagaing dextral corridor, Shan-Thai extrusion faults.
source_derived_tectonic_context: Published Myanmar synthesis distinguishes subduction/collision, Sagaing dextral motion and left-lateral faults around Shan Plateau/northern Laos/Thailand.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Do not classify by nearest boundary alone. Need source-specific fault/megathrust polygons, moment tensor, depth and event location relative to structures.
supporting_references: Wang et al. (2014), JGR Solid Earth; USGS / peer-reviewed Myanmar tectonics reviews.

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 79 candidate events; 59 events in the old Japan–Kuril rectangle are not tagged to this candidate family; 10 events in the box are unassigned.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP AS SEPARATE ARC CANDIDATE; do not treat the entire old Japan–Kuril rectangle as the Kuril–Kamchatka domain.
source_derived_tectonic_context: USGS defines the arc from Hokkaido along the Kurils and Pacific coast of Kamchatka to the Aleutian junction near Commander Islands.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Use a source-backed arc / slab polygon, with explicit southern (Hokkaido) and northern (Aleutian junction) termini; classify interface, intraslab and overriding-plate events separately.

candidate_subdomains: Bering Sea subplate 37; PB2002 western Aleutians orogen 8 (overlapping flags)
observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 37 Bering Sea subplate events total: 12 inside Japan–Kuril rectangle and 25 outside; 8 Western Aleutians orogen events separately flagged.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: DO NOT POOL AUTOMATICALLY WITH KURIL–KAMCHATKA. Retain Aleutian arc and Bering basin/plate as separate review layers; treat the Commander Islands junction explicitly.
source_derived_tectonic_context: USGS describes two Aleutian arc segments meeting near Unimak Pass and distinguishes the Bering Sea margin/shelf.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Need geologic arc extent and slab-zone geometry; Bering Sea subplate membership is not equivalent to Aleutian arc membership. Resolve junction events separately.
supporting_references: Vallier et al., USGS geologic framework of Aleutian arc; USGS Aleutian basin research.

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 11 candidate events distributed across the old Japan–Kuril, Sunda and outside-pilot assignments (3, 5 and 3 respectively).
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP SEPARATE FROM JAPAN/KURIL, SUNDA AND IBM ARCS.
source_derived_tectonic_context: The Ryukyu trench accommodates Philippine Sea Plate subduction beneath Eurasia; Izu-Bonin-Mariana is a distinct Pacific-under-Philippine-Sea system.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Use a Ryukyu-specific trench/slab polygon and explicit northern Taiwan / southern junction limits.

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: Mariana candidate 16; Izu-Bonin candidate 5; Mariana events split between Sunda rectangle and outside-pilot (9 and 7).
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP Izu-Bonin and Mariana as related but separately reviewable arc segments; do not fold into Sunda or Ryukyu.
source_derived_tectonic_context: IBM forearc records Pacific subduction initiation; trench accommodates Pacific subduction beneath Philippine Sea Plate.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Need continuous trench/slab segmentation and depth-based source classification; do not combine merely because the arc system is connected.
supporting_references: Reagan et al. (2023), Earth-Science Reviews; Faccenna et al. (2018).

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: Only 68 candidate tags in old Sunda rectangle; 171 events in the same rectangle are tagged to other candidate families or not the Sunda-arc family.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: SPLIT SUMATRA AND JAVA FOR REVIEW. Do not treat the full Sunda–Indonesia rectangle as one homogeneous system.
source_derived_tectonic_context: Subduction is oblique beneath Sumatra, partitioned by major dextral strike-slip motion; convergence is closer to normal beneath Java.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Use separately defined trench/slab segments and surface fault corridors. Separate megathrust, Sumatran Fault, forearc/backarc and intraslab events if mechanism/depth supports.
supporting_references: Malod et al. (1995); USGS OFR Java; Indonesia seismicity synthesis (2021).

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 36 candidate events tagged across Banda Sea and Timor subdomains.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP SEPARATE FROM SUMATRA/JAVA; evaluate Banda subduction and Timor arc-continent collision as distinct processes or connected subdomains.
source_derived_tectonic_context: The Sunda convergent margin continues eastward as Banda arc; eastern Indonesia involves microplates, collision, subduction, strike-slip and extension.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Need a geologic transition boundary and source type classification; do not let broad plate polygon membership define the whole domain.

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 24 candidate tags; Hasterok family is deliberately distinct from Sunda arc and Banda/Timor groups.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP AS ITS OWN COMPLEX TECTONIC DOMAIN; retain Sangihe and Halmahera flanks as separate subdomains if event counts permit.
source_derived_tectonic_context: Molucca Sea is a rare double-subduction / arc-arc collision system with oppositely dipping slabs.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Need slab geometry and event focal depths/mechanisms; nearest boundary type cannot determine which slab or side generated an event.
supporting_references: Geodynamics of divergent double subduction (2025); Molucca Sea moment tensor study (2021).

candidate_subdomains: Philippine 15; Bicol 11; Mindanao 10; East Luzon 7; West Luzon 3
observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 46 Hasterok candidate-family events; PB2002 Philippines orogen flags 37 events; counts are not identical and layers are not interchangeable.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: KEEP AS COMPLEX UMBRELLA; do not interpret as a single rigid plate or single subduction interface. Subdivide by tectonic subdomain only if event count and authoritative boundaries support it.
source_derived_tectonic_context: Published descriptions identify a mobile belt bounded by opposing-polarity subduction zones with internal collision and strike-slip structures.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Need explicit western/eastern bounding trenches, Philippine Fault, Palawan collision domain and source mechanism/depth. Small subdomain counts require pooling/sensitivity analysis.
supporting_references: The Philippine Mobile Belt (1991); Yumul et al. (2009); MGB Geology of the Philippines.

candidate_subdomains: Central Andes 64 (Puna 46; Altiplano 18); North Andes 8; Peru 6; South Chile 3
observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: Candidate review tags total 81 in these Andes-labelled families; 46 old Andes-box events are flagged as non-Andes/adjacent families; broad South American Plate candidate group is 49 total and must not be equated to the Andes margin.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: REPLACE THE OLD ANDES RECTANGLE WITH PUBLISHED ALONG-STRIKE SEGMENTATION. Keep Northern, Central and Southern Andes / slab segments separate at first; test whether Puna and Altiplano deserve separate analysis.
source_derived_tectonic_context: Nazca slab geometry varies strongly along strike; USGS describes multiple steep and flat-slab segments. Andes tectonic provinces and northern/central/southern domains differ.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Choose one explicit published segment model and translate it into documented polygons. Distinguish interplate, intraslab and crustal Andean events using depth and focal mechanism.
supporting_references: USGS OFR 2015-1031-E; Andean margin tectonic synthesis; Central Andes review (2025).

observed_stage1c2_5_evidence: 584 events have no pre-registered candidate family; 81 outside-pilot events carry candidate tags. Some lie in Bering/Aleutian, Andes/Caribbean, Mariana, Philippine, Scotia or other source units.
provisional_adjudication_recommendation: DO NOT USE AS A CONTROL OR EXCLUDE. Preserve as a discovery / coverage population pending a pre-registered regional scheme.
source_derived_tectonic_context: The GIS sources identify additional active plate and province settings beyond the original four pilot rectangles.
required_evidence_before_freeze: Before selecting controls, define matched non-target controls with comparable data coverage, tectonic type, magnitude completeness, latitude/local-time and seasonal sampling.
supporting_references: All source layers; no single literature region.
